title: Lead Sort By Score
prompt: A lead ranking view needs highest scores first. Write a function that returns a new array sorted by score from highest to lowest without mutating the input.

explanation.beginner:
Example: leadSortByScore([{"id":"a","score":2},{"id":"b","score":5},{"id":"c","score":3}]) produces [{"id":"b","score":5},{"id":"c","score":3},{"id":"a","score":2}]. State the comparison rule and tie behavior explicitly, and copy input before any in-place sort when the contract preserves it.

Compare “handles empty arrays”: input [[]] produces []. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
State the comparison rule and tie behavior explicitly, and copy input before any in-place sort when the contract preserves it.

Tempting mistake: A boolean comparator is not a valid three-way numeric comparator. Equal keys also need a predictable tie policy.

The reference uses sort. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.
